summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and prior crack cocaine use was admitted for acute shortness of breath and reduced exercise tolerance. He reported orthopnea, leg swelling, and a dry cough, with recent high-salt food intake. Initial evaluation showed pulmonary edema on imaging and elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure. He was treated with IV diuretics and nebulizers in the ED, then required BiPAP for respiratory support and was transferred to the ICU. Due to concern for crack-related pneumonitis, he received a course of steroids and antibiotics. His condition improved with treatment, and he was weaned off BiPAP. Repeat imaging showed resolving pulmonary edema, viral studies were negative, and urine culture showed no infection. He was discharged home with a short course of prednisone, instructions to continue heart and diabetes medications, strict low-salt diet, daily weight monitoring, and close outpatient follow-up.
